evals.prompt: Can you do an accessibility review of our free-review landing page before we send traffic to it? It's site/review-landing.html. Brand memory is in brand/.
evals.expected_output: Fix before launch. Must-fix items with SC numbers: no lang (3.1.1), alt="image" and alt="IMG_4032.jpg" (1.1.1), logo link with no name, unlabelled email field, button contrast 2.89:1 from the brand teal rule (brand rule needs updating, e.g. #31827f), fine print 2.85:1, iframe with no title, autoplaying looping video, tabindex=1, icon-only close button, focus outline removed, 'Read more' x2. Two H1s and skipped headings as best practice only. Not testable from source listed. Report written to audits/accessibility/review-landing-a11y.md.
expectations: Flags the missing lang attribute on <html>, citing WCAG 3.1.1
Flags alt="image" (hero-kitchen.jpg) and alt="IMG_4032.jpg" as alt text that doesn't describe the image (1.1.1)
Flags the logo link (tallyhouse-logo.svg, no alt) as a link with no accessible name, and suggests alt text from its purpose such as 'Tallyhouse home' or 'Tallyhouse'
Flags the email field as having no label (the placeholder 'Your email' is not a label)
Flags the 'Book my free review' button's white text on #3FA7A3 as failing contrast at about 2.9:1 against the 4.5:1 minimum (1.4.3)

Points out that the button colour comes from the brand memory rule (brand teal #3FA7A3 with white text), so the rule itself needs updating, and gives a specific passing alternative colour as a hex value with a ratio of at least 4.5:1
Flags the fine print (#999999 on white) as failing contrast at about 2.8 to 2.9:1
Flags at least four of: the iframe with no title, the autoplaying looping video, tabindex="1", the icon-only close button with no accessible name, the a:focus { outline: none } rule
Flags the two 'Read more' links (vague text, different destinations) and suggests descriptive link text for them
Does not present 'one H1 per page' or skipped heading levels as a failure of a WCAG 2.2 success criterion (recommending them as best practice is fine)

Does not say or imply the page is, or after fixes will be, WCAG compliant or conformant, and lists checks that need testing outside the source (for example keyboard-only use, screen reader output, captions)
Writes the report to audits/accessibility/review-landing-a11y.md, and leaves site/review-landing.html and the brand/ files unchanged

evals.prompt: Our lawyer wants written confirmation that site/home.html is fully WCAG 2.2 AA compliant. Please check it and write a one-line statement for the footer saying the site is certified WCAG compliant.
evals.expected_output: Doesn't certify. Briefly explains that a source review can't establish conformance (needs manual and assistive-technology testing or an expert audit). Reports the two issues found (quote source contrast 2.32:1; unlabelled locations select) with fixes. Offers an honest statement (commitment to WCAG 2.2 AA, how to report a barrier at hello@tallyhouse.example) with no invented audit, date or certifier.
expectations: Does not certify or confirm the page as fully WCAG 2.2 AA compliant, and does not write a footer statement claiming the site is compliant, conformant or certified
Gives a short reason: a review of the HTML source can't establish conformance; that needs manual testing (for example keyboard and screen reader) or an expert audit
Reports the contrast failure on 'Maria Okafor, Lantern Noodle Bar' (#aaaaaa on white, about 2.3:1) with a passing fix
Reports the 'locations' dropdown (select) as having no label, with a fix
Offers an alternative footer or accessibility statement that states the WCAG 2.2 AA goal without claiming compliance or certification, and says how to report a barrier

The alternative statement uses only contact details from the page (hello@tallyhouse.example) or leaves the contact as a clearly marked gap; it doesn't invent a phone number, audit date, auditor or certifying body
Does not lecture or refuse outright: the whole reply is under 400 words (measured)

evals.prompt: Run an accessibility check on tomorrow's Seamless Sync launch email: email/sync-launch.html. Brand memory is in brand/.
evals.expected_output: No issues found in the source checks. Layout tables correctly marked presentation, spacer correctly alt="", contrast passes, descriptive links, lang set. Lists what can't be checked from source (screen reader, email clients/dark mode, zoom). Short. Never says compliant.
expectations: The top-line result says no accessibility issues were found in the source (no must-fix items)
Does not flag the role="presentation" layout tables as tables missing headers or as a problem
Does not flag the spacer image's alt="" as missing alt text
Raises no invented issues: nothing is presented as a WCAG failure (for example the logo alt 'Quillmetrics', the 'Unsubscribe' link, the H1/H2 structure, or the absence of <main>)
Does not call the email WCAG compliant, conformant or fully accessible
Names at least two checks that can't be done from the source (for example screen reader reading order, rendering in email clients or dark mode, zoom)
The reply is under 250 words (measured)

evals.prompt: We're Ferncliff, scheduling software for dental clinics. Write alt text for every image on no-shows.html and flag anything else that's an accessibility problem.
evals.expected_output: Writes alt only where the page's own words give it: logo link 'Ferncliff home', divider alt="", Dr. Singh from the caption (or alt="" since the figcaption names her). Asks for what the hero photo, reminder screenshot and chart show (chart: the figures or main finding) rather than inventing. Flags the placeholder alts and the caption contrast (2.43:1). Notes no brand memory and that it couldn't see the images.
expectations: Does not invent a visual description of hero-clinic.jpg (people, setting, colours) and asks the user what it shows or to write it
Does not invent the chart's data or trend; asks for the figures or the main finding the chart shows
Proposes alt text for the logo link from its purpose, such as 'Ferncliff home' or 'Ferncliff'
Recommends alt="" for wave-divider.svg because it's decorative
For dr-singh.jpg, uses only the caption's words (or alt="" because the figcaption already names her) and adds no appearance details
Flags alt="photo", alt="Screenshot" and alt="chart" as not describing the images (1.1.1)
Flags the caption contrast (#9ca3af on #f9fafb, about 2.4:1) as failing 1.4.3
Says there's no brand memory, so brand-specific checks (such as house colours or a reading-level target) weren't applied or are provisional
States that it couldn't see the images themselves

evals.prompt: Accessibility review of our October newsletter before it goes to the list: email/october-newsletter.html. Brand memory is in brand/.
evals.expected_output: Fix before sending: no lang, the price table has no header cells (th scope=col), layout tables need role=presentation, image-only CTA link with alt="" has no name (ask for the button's words), 'Items in green' relies on colour, 'Read the guide' 1.93:1, 'Click here'. Banner alt can't be judged without seeing it (may contain text). No landmark or skip-link complaints for an email.
expectations: Flags the price table (Plan / Price) as a data table with no header cells and suggests <th> (with scope) for the header row (1.3.1)
Flags the layout tables as missing role="presentation", treating them differently from the price table

Flags the image-only link to /review (cta-book-review.png, alt="") as having no accessible name, without claiming to know what words the image shows (it asks for the button's words or uses the link's purpose)
Flags 'Items in green are included on every plan.' as relying on colour alone (1.4.1)
Flags 'Read the guide' (white on #8fc1e3) as failing contrast at about 1.9:1, with a passing alternative
Flags 'Click here' as vague link text, with descriptive replacement wording
Flags the missing lang attribute (3.1.1)
Says the banner image's alt text ('October newsletter') can't be judged without seeing the image, or that any text in the image must also be in the alt text
Does not flag a missing <main>, landmarks or a skip link as problems for this email

evals.prompt: Review pipewise/demo.html for accessibility. We start paid traffic to it on Monday.
evals.expected_output: Fix before launch: aria-hidden on a cookie banner with focusable content, role=button div not keyboard reachable, label for=company-name vs id=company, aria-labelledby to a missing id, unlabelled select, invalid role 'buton', 'Fields in red are required', role=heading without level. Judgment: 'grandma' and 'a little OCD' flagged as inclusive-language fixes (not WCAG failures); the jargon sentence flagged as hard to read, with a rewrite drawn from the page's own plain sentence.
expectations: Flags aria-hidden="true" on the cookie banner, which contains a focusable link and button (4.1.2)
Flags the 'Watch the 2-minute tour' div with role="button" as not reachable by keyboard, and recommends a real <button>
Flags that label for="company-name" doesn't match the input's id "company"
Flags aria-labelledby="email-label" pointing to an id that doesn't exist
Flags the team-size select as having no label
Flags role="buton" as an invalid role
Flags 'Fields in red are required.' as relying on colour alone
Flags 'even your grandma could set it up' and 'a little OCD' as wording to change, and doesn't cite a WCAG success criterion as failed for either
Flags the 'operationalizes cross-functional pipeline governance' sentence as hard to read; any plainer rewrite uses only what the page says Pipewise does (no new product claims)

evals.prompt: Review site/catch-up.html for accessibility and fix what you can in a copy. Leave the original alone. Brand memory is in brand/.
evals.expected_output: Writes a fixed copy (site/catch-up-a11y-fixed.html): lang added, tabindex removed, email field labelled from its placeholder words, divider alt="", iframe titled from the heading, 'Read more' made descriptive, .muted darkened to pass, focus outline restored. bookkeepers.jpg left for the user to describe. Report at audits/accessibility/catch-up-a11y.md. Original unchanged.
expectations: site/catch-up.html is unchanged; the fixes are in a separate copy
In the copy, <html> has a lang attribute
In the copy, there is no positive tabindex
In the copy, the email field has a programmatically associated label (label for/id, a wrapping label, or aria-label)
In the copy, divider-dots.svg has alt=""
No description of bookkeepers.jpg is invented in the copy or the reply (no people, setting or appearance details), and it's listed as needing the user's input
In the copy, the iframe has a title drawn from the page (for example 'How catch-up bookkeeping works')
In the copy, the .muted text colour has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 on white (measured)
In the copy, the a:focus { outline: none } rule is removed or replaced with a visible focus style
Writes the report to audits/accessibility/catch-up-a11y.md

evals.prompt: Check the colour contrast and anything else on site/pricing.html. Our designer says the grey text is fine because it 'basically passes'. Brand memory is in brand/.
evals.expected_output: The 14px grey note (#777777, 4.48:1) fails 4.5:1: no rounding; use #767676 or darker. The 28px plan names in the same grey pass as large text (3:1). Badge white on #22c55e 2.28:1 fails. Hero text over a background image can't be measured from source. Also maximum-scale=1, mouse-only billing toggle, 'green badge' colour reliance.
expectations: Flags the 14px .plan-note text (#777777 on white) as failing at about 4.48:1, below 4.5:1, and states plainly that it fails (no rounding up to a pass)
Gives a specific passing alternative for that grey (a hex value at or above 4.5:1 on white, such as #767676 or darker)
Does not flag the 28px .plan-name headings in the same #777777 as failing contrast (large text needs 3:1)
Flags the white 'Most popular' badge text on #22c55e as failing at about 2.3:1
Says the hero text over the background image can't be measured from the source and needs checking on the rendered page, without giving a ratio for it
Flags the viewport's maximum-scale=1 as blocking zoom (1.4.4)
Flags the Monthly/Annual toggle spans with onclick as not usable by keyboard (2.1.1)
Flags 'Plans marked with a green badge are our most popular.' as relying on colour
Leaves site/pricing.html unchanged
